title: Owning the result
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you judge people on the task they finished, or on the result they own?

Jose asked: what is the criteria for pushing the limit, for making it shorter? He is not a stainless steel engineer. A student said: I think it is honestly curiosity, the childlike play: stainless works here and we don't have to press it, we could roll it. At the first-principles level it could be the same.
Another student said: perhaps a little perfectionism too: he is trying to maximize the potential of the product. And you can buy the same material for both companies, at a steeper discount, in bulk.

I'm reading between the lines, Jose said, and I'd like to see more evidence. I think he judges people on whether they are prepared to own the result. He asks: is this person going to take accountability and ownership of the result?

His example: I say: you need to make this decision today. I give you alternatives. Are you comfortable with a quota of four million dollars this month? You say: no, I can do two or three. I'm judging you on how you take ownership of the result.
He doesn't look at tasks like other people do, Jose said. He goes beyond completing the task. Are you going to be responsible for the result?
A student agreed: extreme ownership within his organization. Jose said: his organization is all about owning the results. He expects high-impact behaviours and decisions, not low or medium impact.
What result do you want each person to own?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the result you want each person on your team to own.
Write how you would ask them if they will.
Write the quota or target you would negotiate with them.
Write what you would do if someone only finishes tasks.
Write the difference between a task and a result in your work.

check.q: What did Jose say he thinks the person judges people on?
choices: Whether they will own the result

check.q: What did a student say may be behind the decisions?
What did Jose say the person does beyond completing the task?
choices: Asks if you will be responsible for the result

recap: Judge on the result owned, not the task finished. Be honest that it is your reading.
